trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out down or around the edge to (5,2) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
The line must go right: up is number 10, which comes later; down is number 4, which comes later.
Going down would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
Going up, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,1). So the line goes around the edge to (2,1).
The line must go down: up is number 9, which comes later.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going right would force the line onto number 6 before its turn. So the line goes down.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Cell (3,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going around the edge to (4,1) would force the line onto number 8 before its turn. So the line goes down.

Going around the edge to (1,5) would force the line onto number 9 before its turn; going around the edge to (5,1) would leave both number 9 and cell (4,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes left.
Going around the edge to (1,4) would leave number 8 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes left.
The line must go left: around the edge to (1,3) is number 10, which comes later.
Going left would leave both number 9 and cell (4,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 40 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 15 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 20/25 cells (80%).
Generation 2: fitness 14/25. The best line covers 21 cells, the first 14 of them still look solvable.
Generation 4: fitness 25/25. The best line covers 25 cells.
Generation 4: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Tried 48 futures: 79% survive going down (best covers 56%); around the edge to (5,2) 0%.
Tried 48 futures: 79% survive going right (best covers 36%); down 0%.
Tried 72 futures: 83% survive going right (best covers 56%); up 0%; down 0%.
Tried 48 futures: 0% survive going around the edge to (2,1) (best covers 36%); up 0%.
Tried 48 futures: 0% survive going right (best covers 36%); down 0%.
Jackpot! A future after going down covers the whole board. Cashing in!
